title: Not being involved in the jazz scene
summary: He and Kirchner discuss how jazz news in New York passes him by.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: You've been telling me about the life of jazz in New York; I was not aware of it. More had been going on, because I thought it was nothing; you never hear of it. I don't know why, but I have never really been that involved with jazz. That's not right either. Something's wrong. Why? I don't know.
I don't know if it's a question of right or wrong. From my own standpoint, if you get involved in the

New York scene as far as Jazz goes, you make it a point to know what's happening just because you're part of that, but from what I've been able to observe in various people who I respect, it's very easy to get away from that, if you're not really immersed in it.

You can only be immersed in it if you're working in it and that didn't happen. And then for publicity and even in clubs, when you read the reviews in the New York Times, it's never that. It's occasionally Zoot and Al or Stan at a club somewhere.
Yeah, you read about established people, you don't read about up and coming people that much, except somebody who becomes the darling of the critics or something like that.
Let's see, let's get back to Benny again.
